pure-announcement.rationale: This is Vercel's own launch post ('Today we're open sourcing deepsec') built of testimonials, screenshots and npx setup steps, and its five one-line workflow bullets describe the product rather than teach a technique that stands apart from it.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers agentic security scanning of codebases; the overlap with existing MCP and sandbox notes is topical only.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The tool is open source and runnable, so its behaviour is checkable even though the false-positive rate and customer claims are vendor-reported.

durability.rationale: Its substance is launch-moment specifics — Opus 4.7 at max effort, GPT 5.5 at xhigh, a 10-20% false-positive rate, current sandbox scaling — that will be stale well inside twelve months.

actionability.rationale: The only actions offered are product-only steps (npx deepsec init, write custom matchers for this tool), with the scan-investigate-revalidate pattern never developed enough to reproduce independently.

atomicity.rationale: It is one idea — an agent-driven security scanning harness run on your own infrastructure — statable in a single paragraph.
